Jordan — thanks for the clear examples, and appreciate the spreadsheet. Attaching a CSV with some worked numbers (redwood-billing-examples.csv). High level answers up front, then I put concrete line-item examples below.

High level:
- Token accounting: we bill on tokens generated + input tokens. When KV cache or prefix is reused, we do not double-charge tokens that are served from a cached KV entry in the same session — we bill the incremental new tokens required to extend the KV cache, not the full original prefix every time.
- Rounding window: default is per-inference request rounding to the nearest billing quantum (our quantum = 64-token unit) for hosted requests; for streaming we apply rounding at the stream flush boundary (when the stream completes or when a 1-minute soft-flush happens). For long-running sessions that keep a warm KV cache across minute boundaries, we charge the cache warmup once per session lifecycle and then only incremental increments after that.
- Pilot floor: we can offer a monthly pilot floor (committed tokens) with a blended discount and credits for unused reserved capacity.

Quick worked example (based on rows in your spreadsheet):
1) Short ad-hoc calls (70% of traffic): 1k requests/day at median 120 tokens per request -> invoiced as 120 tokens rounded up to nearest 64 -> 128 tokens/request.
2) Long sessions (30% traffic): 300 sessions/day with a 100k token context reused across sequential messages. For each session we bill initial context ingest (100k tokens) once, amortized across session lifetime; subsequent messages within same session only bill incremental output tokens + any new input. If a session re-creates KV (session restart) within the same billing day, the initial ingest is re-billed.

Illustrative math (simplified):
- Short calls: 1,000 * 128 = 128,000 tokens/day
- Long sessions: 300 * (initial 100,000 amortized over 10 messages -> 10,000 per message equivalent) = 300 * 10,000 = 3,000,000 tokens/day (amortized)
- Combined daily: 3,128,000 tokens -> monthly (~22 working days) = ~68,816,000 tokens.

Rounding nuance: because short calls individually round up to 128 tokens, there's a small rounding overhead; for long sessions the amortization smooths rounding. If you want to avoid per-call rounding overhead we can suggest batching short calls (your app can bundle 2-3 requests) or enabling a session-level micro-batching feature.

Pilot pricing proposal (preliminary):
- Commitment: 5M tokens/month reserved for 3 months (pilot)
- Pilot discount: 12% effective discount on per-token list price for committed tokens in month 1; unused committed tokens at month-end can be credited back up to 30% of unused amount (to reduce waste).
- Overages: billed at standard per-token rate with per-request rounding rules above.

I'll loop Vanessa and Marissa for any policy tweaks or special SOW language. If you'd like a side-by-side sample invoice, we can produce one for the April 1 week in your sheet.

Thanks — Sean

Looping in Marissa for finance/discount guidance. A few internal notes: 

- Policy: standard pilot commit minimum is 2M tokens/month; we can stretch to 5M for strategic deals but need explicit rollback terms after 3 months.
- Credit rules: we allow up to 30% carry-back on unused committed tokens across the pilot period but not beyond the pilot term. Any carryback reduces the effective commit for next billing period.
- Rounding exceptions: we can include a one-off invoice-level rounding reconciliation for the pilot (finance will do month-end true-up) to smooth the small per-request rounding overhead Jordan mentions. That helps procurement.
- Commercial ask: if Acme wants a larger credit (40% unused), we need a 6-month commitment and a 15% minimum ARR uplift target.

Suggested message to customer: propose the 5M token pilot with 12% first-quarter discount, include month-end rounding true-up for the pilot, and attach a draft SOW. I'll approve the SOW text changes if Sean includes the rollback and credit caps.

Jordan — thanks for the patience. Per our internal review here's a concise proposal and a couple of concrete invoice-style examples attached in the SOW PDF. Key points first:

Proposal summary:
- Pilot term: 3 months (May–July 2027)
- Committed capacity: 5,000,000 tokens/month
- Pilot discount: 12% effective discount on committed tokens for the first month; months 2–3 at 8% (blended effective ~9.3%)
- Unused committed tokens: up to 30% refundable/creditable at month-end during pilot; for any single month above 30% unused, standard overage policy applies to the deficit
- Rounding & token accounting: we will bill per-request rounded to 64-token quantum for non-streaming calls; for streaming calls we bill on stream flush boundary with minute-soft-flush semantics. KV/prefix reuse within the same session will not re-bill the entire prefix — only incremental tokens required when the cache grows. We will perform a month-end true-up to reconcile rounding differences for this pilot.

Example invoice snippets (simplified):
- Day sample A (mostly short calls): 1,000 requests * 128 tokens rounded = 128k tokens/day -> 2.8M tokens/month equivalent
- Day sample B (long sessions): 300 sessions with amortized initial ingest = ~3.0M tokens/day -> large amortization; see attached SOW for line-by-line numbers pulled from your spreadsheet.
